Dt:09.08.2024 1) The petitioners through the medium of instant petition have challenged the proceedings filed by the respondent against them under Section 12 of the Protection Of Women From Domestic Violence Act (hereinafter "the D.V.Act").

entities.text: Protection Of Women From Domestic Violence Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Challenge has also been thrown to order dated 04.08.2023 passed by learned Chief Judicial Magistrate Handwara, whereby the petitioners herein have been restrained from committing any act of domestic violence upon the respondent and they have also been directed to provide separate residential accommodation in shared house hold to the respondent.
2) Issue notice to the respondent.

3) Mr.S.M.S.Geelani, Advocate appears and accepts notice on behalf of the respondent.
4) Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of 5) It has been contended by learned counsel for the petitioners that soon after the marriage of petitioner No.1 with the respondent, she left the company of petitioner No.1 as he did not accede to her request to reside separately from his parents.
It has been contended that when petitioner No.1 approached the respondent to return to the matrimonial home, she did not return.

It has also been contended that the respondent has filed proceedings under Section 125 Cr.P.C against petitioner No.1 and she is getting monthly maintenance of Rs.5000/- from him pursuant to the orders passed in the said proceedings.
It has also been contended that the respondent has registered an FIR against the petitioners for offences under Section 498A IPC.

According to the petitioners the Mudasir Ali Mir And Ors vs Sameena Begum on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95254659/
1 allegations made in the impugned petition are absolutely false and that the said petition has been made just to harass them.
6) If we have a look at the impugned order dated 04.08.2023 passed by learned trial Magistrate, it appears that although the same has been passed after hearing the parties, yet the petitioners had yet to file their reply to the petition under Section 12 of the D.V.Act filed by the respondent against them.

entities.text: Mudasir Ali Mir And Ors vs Sameena Begum on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It seems that the petitioners were granted an opportunity to file objections to the petition but they did not file the same, as a result of which learned trial Magistrate was constrained to consider grant of interim relief in the absence of the reply of the petitioners.
Accordingly, order dated 04.08.2023 came to be passed.
CM(M) No.56/2024 P a g e | 2 of 3  7)

Having regard to the fact that the version pr petition by the petitioners was not before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate when the impugned order dated 04.08.2023 was passed, it would be appropriate to allow the petitioners to file their objections to the petition under Section 12 of the D.V.Act filed by the respondent against them before the trial Magistrate, so that the same is considered and a fresh order is passed by the learned trial Magistrate.

8) In view of the above, this petition is disposed of with liberty to the petitioners to file reply to the petition under Section 12 of the D.V.Act filed by the respondent against them before the learned trial Magistrate, whereafter the learned Magistrate shall accord fresh consideration to the case upon hearing both the parties.
Thereafter a fresh order regarding grant of interim relief shall be passed by the trial Magistrate.

The petitioners are also at liberty to file an application for dropping of proceedings against them before the trial Magistrate, which shall also be considered by the said Magistrate after hearing the parties.
Till such time a fresh order is passed by the learned trial Magistrate, the impugned order dated 04.08.2023 shall remain in operation.
(SANJAY DHAR) JUDGE SRINAGAR 09.08.2024
